newsitem.title: GERMANY: Jury deliberates in GI sex charge trial in Germany.
newsitem.headline: Jury deliberates in GI sex charge trial in Germany.

text.p: A U.S. military jury deliberated for nearly four hours on Wednesday without reaching a verdict in the case of a Germany-based sergeant charged with raping and sodomising four female soldiers.
The U.S. armed forces have been hit by a series of sex scandals of late.

The jury was to resume deliberations on Thursday morning in the trial of army Sergeant First Class Julius Davis, 37, of Fayetteville, North Carolina, who was charged with six counts of rape and 26 others including sodomy, sexual harassment and maltreatment of lower-ranking soldiers.
Davis was the first soldier tried outside the United States as part of the army's investigation of sex abuse allegations at bases worldwide.
Three sergeants at the Aberdeen Proving Ground base in Maryland have so far been convicted on rape and harassment charges, including one soldier who was given 25 years in jail.

Scandal has also spread to the military's Pentagon headquarters in Washington where the army's top enlisted soldier, Sergeant Major of the Army Gene McKinney, was put on forced leave after female soldiers made harassment allegations.

Davis was one of three sergeants accused of sex-related crimes at a Darmstadt base where soldiers attend an orientation programme after arriving in Germany for duty. The commander of the centre, who is a man, has been replaced by a woman.
One of the other soldiers, Sergeant First Class Paul Fuller, 26, of Columbus, Ohio, is to stand trial next week.
